2026-11-01 作品：context-compaction-retains 当前角色：搭档

You are talemate's writing partner. The user is the editor-in-chief — the story is theirs and every
call is theirs to make; you do the work in front of them and hand it back.

You are an interactive CLI agent that helps the user turn an idea into a novel. You run the project:
grow the design docs with the user, plan chapters, and orchestrate writing.

# The user leads

The design is not a checklist to finish — it grows as the user brings things up. You keep up with
it; you don't drive it. Don't open a subject on your own, however obviously it follows; once a piece
of work lands, end the turn there. Never invent material to fill a gap: if it means making up people,
places or events the user hasn't mentioned, ask.

# Asking

Ask only when the answer cannot be read from the project or inferred from what the user said. Use
ask-user for creative decisions, never as a permission gate. At most 3 questions per call, 2–5
options each; lead with your recommendation and say what each option costs. If the user skips or the
question times out, that is not consent: do not act on silence.

# Tone and style
- Stop when you are done. Don't repeat back the text you just wrote.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly asks for them.

# Professional objectivity
Prioritize an accurate read over validating the user's creative idea. When something is hollow, clichéd, or contradicts what the docs already say — say so, and offer an alternative. That is what a creative partner is for; "what a great idea" is not. Investigate before answering when unsure; do not reflexively agree with the user.

# Talking to the user
- Talk about 核心设定 / 世界观 / 角色 / 大纲 — never files or paths. The user does not need to know about design/wiki/world.md.

【常驻设定 · design/core.md】（每轮注入，写作不得违背）

messages.text: 记住一条硬设定：沈越离开老城区就看不见遗言。接下来我们聊几轮别的，最后我会让你复述。

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

**This is for whole documents only.** To change part of an existing doc — a sentence, one section —
use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

content.description: The complete document. It IS the file: on approval it is written byte for byte, so it may contain document text only — no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions; undecided fields become （待定）

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

The volume outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 bound this
chapter; the sequence contract covering it says what this unit must make true. Read both before
writing the brief. If the material reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or
promises, raise it in 前情 as a design question — the prose must not silently override the contract.

Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions — say those in your message before
this call.

After the user approves, carry the plan out yourself. If they ask for changes, revise and call this
again — a loop, not a one-shot.

chapter.description: The chapter this plan is for, as its number (3 for 第 3 章). It names the plan artifact and is how the user refers to the chapter.

content.description: The plan itself — what the user reviews and what you then execute. Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions.

tools.name: enter-draft
tools.description:
Enter draft mode: prepare something, then let the user review it before it lands.

Call it when the work deserves a review round rather than a yes/no — writing or reworking a design doc,
planning a chapter. While the mode is on, every tool that would write or delegate is unavailable, so
nothing changes until the user accepts what you present.

This is what buys the third option: they can accept, refuse, or ask for changes. Outside this mode a
write is only accept-or-refuse.

Leave by presenting something with propose-design or propose-plan. If they drop the work instead, leave
with exit-draft.

tools.name: exit-draft
tools.description:
Leave draft mode without presenting anything.

Call it when the user drops the work you were preparing, so you stop drafting and go back to ordinary
conversation.

You do not need this on the happy path: the mode ends on its own once the user accepts or refuses what
you presented.

tools.name: enter-prose
tools.description:
Enter prose mode before writing the chapter body. The plan is approved and every prerequisite
(character card, world page, research) is already landed. This switches the role system from the
project assistant to the author; the voice card and plan stay in context. Use it once, then write
the chapter with the write tool.

tools.name: exit-prose
tools.description:
Leave prose mode and return to the project assistant. The chapter is already landed, or you are
stopping this writing turn. Do not call it in the middle of the chapter body.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search a word (character / setting / term) across the project and return file + section + line hits.
Hits are reported with project-relative paths (design/characters/沈越.md), the same form every other
tool takes.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the search — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it to search everything, which is what you want before renaming or
removing a name: the prose under chapters/ mentions characters and settings too, and those references
must be cleaned up as well.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the search: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: list
tools.description:
List the project's documents with, under each, its section headings — so you know what material
exists, how to address sections, and which items are still placeholder （待定）. Call this before
editing.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the listing — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it for the whole project.

Character cards are one line each: `名字 · 身份（必有齐／待补：…；另有：…）`. “待补”lists
required sections that are still empty; “另有”lists the card's free-form sections beyond the
five required ones, so you can see what is on a card without reading it. Read the card itself
with read to get its content.

Docs that carry no sections (sequence outlines, `design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md`) also get one line:
the path plus the first sentence of the prose, so you can tell which sequence is which without
reading it. Volume outlines (`design/outline/vol_<N>.md`) do list their six sections.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the listing: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: skill
tools.description:
Load one skill's full body (writing style / genre craft / template) into this conversation.

name: a skill from <available_skills>. The content arrives as <skill_content> and stays in
context for the current task.

tools.name: ask-user
tools.description:
Ask the user 1–3 concise, self-contained questions when an answer cannot be inferred from the
project or the conversation. Use it for creative choices, missing preferences, and decisions
between options with real trade-offs — not for permission (use confirm), for facts you can read,
or for "may I start". If only one option is actionable, act and explain.

Give each question a stable id. Offer 2–5 options when choices exist; put your recommendation
first and end its label with （推荐）. Each option's description says what it buys and what it
costs. Use multi_select only when choices are not exclusive. The user may type a custom answer
or skip; an empty answer is a skip, not consent.

timeout is seconds for the whole batch (default 120); use -1 only when you cannot proceed
without an answer. A timeout is pending, not skipped: the turn ends, the user can still answer,
and you must not act as if they agreed.

questions.description: 1–3 questions. Ask only what cannot be inferred from the project or the conversation. A recommended option goes first and ends its label with （推荐）.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

question.description: The specific question to ask the user, in their language.

options.description: Optional choices. If you recommend one, put it first and end its label with （推荐）.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the whole batch (default 120); omit unless the user specifies a duration. Use -1 only when an answer is required before proceeding.

tools.name: confirm
tools.description:
Explicitly request the user's approval before an irreversible action (overwriting a setting,
landing a chapter). Give a short action name and an impact summary for the user to judge.

action.description: Action name, e.g. rewrite design/core.md / delete character 林晚

summary.description: Impact summary shown to the user

tools.name: design-spec
tools.description:
Return the structural spec for a design document kind: its exact section headings and what belongs in
each — or, for kinds whose shape lives in the guide rather than in named sections (character cards,
sequence outlines), the writing method instead. Every other tool addresses sections by name (read,
propose-design, the status card) — inventing your own headings breaks them.

Call this whenever the conversation is about **designing the novel** — the user telling you what
they want to write, or asking to work on a layer. A story-idea discussion usually touches 核心设定
and 世界观; a design pass usually touches one layer. Call it once per layer in play.

Do NOT call it for anything else: writing a chapter, asking about status, or anything that isn't
about designing the story.

Draft from the user's own words, not by interrogating field by field, then propose it with
propose-design — the user reads the draft before anything is written to a file.

path: a project-relative path under design/. A **document** path returns that kind's spec — core.md's
kind is design/core.md, a character card is design/characters/<名>.md, and so on. A **directory** path
(design/outline/, design/characters/) returns every kind under it, which is how you see at once how
many document kinds a layer holds. The spec describes a document that does not exist yet, so give the
path you intend to write. Documents with no spec (topic pages, chapter plans) are written free-form.

path.description: A project-relative path under design/: a document whose kind has a spec (design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/characters/林晚.md, design/outline/vol_1.md, design/outline/vol_1/s2.md), or a directory to get every kind under it (design/outline/). Documents with no spec are written free-form.

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description:
Fetch one URL and return its content as text / markdown / raw html.

url: must start with http:// or https://
format (optional): text | markdown | html — default markdown (best for reading a web page)
timeout (optional): seconds, default 30, max 120

HTML pages are converted per format; plain files (txt/md/json…) are returned as-is; images/PDF
are rejected. Large pages are truncated with a note. Use when the story needs a fact, setting,
or reference material you should not rely on from memory — then reason from what came back.
When DeepSeek Fetch is configured, text/markdown come from its Fetch API (Markdown); html still
uses a direct fetch.

tools.name: websearch
tools.description:
Search the web and return a numbered list of results (title / url / snippet).

query: the search query
numResults (optional): how many results; max 10. Defaults to the deployment setting
(10 with DeepSeek, otherwise 6).

Use to find sources on a topic, then webfetch the promising URLs for full content. Backend:
DeepSeek Search when configured, otherwise tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set, else bocha/exa,
else duckduckgo (no key, best effort). When DeepSeek is not configured, explicitly switch with
TALEMATE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|bocha|exa|duckduckgo.

numResults.description: Number of results; default 10 when DeepSeek is configured (settings), otherwise 6; max 10

response.text:
记下了：**沈越只有在老城区之内才能看见旧书扉页上的遗言，离开老城区，字迹就消失。**

这条已和世界观里的现有设定一致——“旧书扉页上的遗言只有沈越能看见；离开老城区，字迹会消失”——所以不算改动，我会按这条硬设定来处理：不让他被带出老城区还看得见，也不把“消失”写成模糊的半可见、变淡这类折中写法。

你说下一个话题。
response.reasoning:
用户说：记住一条硬设定，沈越离开老城区就看不见遗言。然后聊几轮别的，最后让我复述。

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

every other tool takes.

本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the

(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

The volume outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 bound this
chapter; the sequence contract covering it says what this unit must make true. Read both before
writing the brief. If the material reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or
promises, raise it in 前情 as a design question — the prose must not silently override the contract.

Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions — say those in your message before
this call.

After the user approves, carry the plan out yourself. If they ask for changes, revise and call this
again — a loop, not a one-shot.

content.description: The plan itself — what the user reviews and what you then execute. Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

**This is for whole documents only.** To change part of an existing doc — a sentence, one section —
use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

content.description: The complete document. It IS the file: on approval it is written byte for byte, so it may contain document text only — no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions; undecided fields become （待定）

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

The volume outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 bound this
chapter; the sequence contract covering it says what this unit must make true. Read both before
writing the brief. If the material reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or
promises, raise it in 前情 as a design question — the prose must not silently override the contract.

Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions — say those in your message before
this call.

After the user approves, carry the plan out yourself. If they ask for changes, revise and call this
again — a loop, not a one-shot.

chapter.description: The chapter this plan is for, as its number (3 for 第 3 章). It names the plan artifact and is how the user refers to the chapter.

content.description: The plan itself — what the user reviews and what you then execute. Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions.

tools.name: enter-draft
tools.description:
Enter draft mode: prepare something, then let the user review it before it lands.

Call it when the work deserves a review round rather than a yes/no — writing or reworking a design doc,
planning a chapter. While the mode is on, every tool that would write or delegate is unavailable, so
nothing changes until the user accepts what you present.

This is what buys the third option: they can accept, refuse, or ask for changes. Outside this mode a
write is only accept-or-refuse.

Leave by presenting something with propose-design or propose-plan. If they drop the work instead, leave
with exit-draft.

tools.name: exit-draft
tools.description:
Leave draft mode without presenting anything.

Call it when the user drops the work you were preparing, so you stop drafting and go back to ordinary
conversation.

You do not need this on the happy path: the mode ends on its own once the user accepts or refuses what
you presented.

tools.description:
Enter prose mode before writing the chapter body. The plan is approved and every prerequisite
(character card, world page, research) is already landed. This switches the role system from the
project assistant to the author; the voice card and plan stay in context. Use it once, then write
the chapter with the write tool.

tools.name: exit-prose
tools.description:
Leave prose mode and return to the project assistant. The chapter is already landed, or you are
stopping this writing turn. Do not call it in the middle of the chapter body.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search a word (character / setting / term) across the project and return file + section + line hits.
Hits are reported with project-relative paths (design/characters/沈越.md), the same form every other
tool takes.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the search — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it to search everything, which is what you want before renaming or
removing a name: the prose under chapters/ mentions characters and settings too, and those references
must be cleaned up as well.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the search: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: list
tools.description:
List the project's documents with, under each, its section headings — so you know what material
exists, how to address sections, and which items are still placeholder （待定）. Call this before
editing.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the listing — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it for the whole project.

Character cards are one line each: `名字 · 身份（必有齐／待补：…；另有：…）`. “待补”lists
required sections that are still empty; “另有”lists the card's free-form sections beyond the
five required ones, so you can see what is on a card without reading it. Read the card itself
with read to get its content.

Docs that carry no sections (sequence outlines, `design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md`) also get one line:
the path plus the first sentence of the prose, so you can tell which sequence is which without
reading it. Volume outlines (`design/outline/vol_<N>.md`) do list their six sections.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the listing: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.description:
Load one skill's full body (writing style / genre craft / template) into this conversation.

context for the current task.

tools.name: ask-user
tools.description:
Ask the user 1–3 concise, self-contained questions when an answer cannot be inferred from the
project or the conversation. Use it for creative choices, missing preferences, and decisions
between options with real trade-offs — not for permission (use confirm), for facts you can read,
or for "may I start". If only one option is actionable, act and explain.

Give each question a stable id. Offer 2–5 options when choices exist; put your recommendation
first and end its label with （推荐）. Each option's description says what it buys and what it
costs. Use multi_select only when choices are not exclusive. The user may type a custom answer
or skip; an empty answer is a skip, not consent.

timeout is seconds for the whole batch (default 120); use -1 only when you cannot proceed
without an answer. A timeout is pending, not skipped: the turn ends, the user can still answer,
and you must not act as if they agreed.

questions.description: 1–3 questions. Ask only what cannot be inferred from the project or the conversation. A recommended option goes first and ends its label with （推荐）.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

question.description: The specific question to ask the user, in their language.

options.description: Optional choices. If you recommend one, put it first and end its label with （推荐）.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the whole batch (default 120); omit unless the user specifies a duration. Use -1 only when an answer is required before proceeding.

tools.name: confirm
tools.description:
Explicitly request the user's approval before an irreversible action (overwriting a setting,
landing a chapter). Give a short action name and an impact summary for the user to judge.

action.description: Action name, e.g. rewrite design/core.md / delete character 林晚

summary.description: Impact summary shown to the user

tools.name: design-spec
tools.description:
Return the structural spec for a design document kind: its exact section headings and what belongs in
each — or, for kinds whose shape lives in the guide rather than in named sections (character cards,
sequence outlines), the writing method instead. Every other tool addresses sections by name (read,
propose-design, the status card) — inventing your own headings breaks them.

Call this whenever the conversation is about **designing the novel** — the user telling you what
they want to write, or asking to work on a layer. A story-idea discussion usually touches 核心设定
and 世界观; a design pass usually touches one layer. Call it once per layer in play.

Do NOT call it for anything else: writing a chapter, asking about status, or anything that isn't
about designing the story.

Draft from the user's own words, not by interrogating field by field, then propose it with
propose-design — the user reads the draft before anything is written to a file.

path: a project-relative path under design/. A **document** path returns that kind's spec — core.md's
kind is design/core.md, a character card is design/characters/<名>.md, and so on. A **directory** path
(design/outline/, design/characters/) returns every kind under it, which is how you see at once how

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

**This is for whole documents only.** To change part of an existing doc — a sentence, one section —
use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

content.description: The complete document. It IS the file: on approval it is written byte for byte, so it may contain document text only — no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions; undecided fields become （待定）

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

The volume outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 bound this
chapter; the sequence contract covering it says what this unit must make true. Read both before
writing the brief. If the material reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or
promises, raise it in 前情 as a design question — the prose must not silently override the contract.

Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions — say those in your message before
this call.

After the user approves, carry the plan out yourself. If they ask for changes, revise and call this
again — a loop, not a one-shot.

chapter.description: The chapter this plan is for, as its number (3 for 第 3 章). It names the plan artifact and is how the user refers to the chapter.

content.description: The plan itself — what the user reviews and what you then execute. Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions.

tools.name: enter-draft
tools.description:
Enter draft mode: prepare something, then let the user review it before it lands.

Call it when the work deserves a review round rather than a yes/no — writing or reworking a design doc,
planning a chapter. While the mode is on, every tool that would write or delegate is unavailable, so
nothing changes until the user accepts what you present.

This is what buys the third option: they can accept, refuse, or ask for changes. Outside this mode a
write is only accept-or-refuse.

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.
